options.label: A fluid transported in a plant's xylem or phloem cells
options.feedback: Correct. Sap moves water and nutrients through specialized cells in the plant.

options.label: The sticky substance that oozes from a wounded tree
options.feedback: That describes resin, which is a separate substance from sap.

options.label: The milky liquid found in some plant cells
options.feedback: That is latex, a different product from sap.

options.label: The watery content inside a single plant cell
options.feedback: That is cell sap, not the sap that travels through the plant's transport system.

items.ok_line: Sap is the fluid moving through xylem and phloem.
items.ko_line: That is a different plant product, not sap.
items.exp_text: Sap is the fluid that travels in the xylem or phloem cells of a plant, carrying water and nutrients. It is not latex, resin, or cell sap, which are produced separately and have different compositions and jobs.

items.prompt: Which two main types of sap are there in a plant?

options.label: Latex sap and resin sap
options.feedback: Latex and resin are not types of sap; the two types are xylem sap and phloem sap.

options.label: Root sap and leaf sap
options.feedback: Sap is not classified by where it is; the two types are xylem sap and phloem sap.

options.label: Water sap and sugar sap
options.feedback: That describes their contents but is not the official classification; the two types are xylem sap and phloem sap.

options.label: Xylem sap and phloem sap
options.feedback: Correct. These are the two broad categories of sap.

items.ok_line: Sap comes as xylem sap and phloem sap.
items.ko_line: Those are not the two main types.
items.exp_text: Sap is divided into two broad types: xylem sap and phloem sap. Each travels through its own set of cells and carries different materials.

items.prompt: What does xylem sap mainly consist of?

options.label: A thick sugary solution
options.feedback: That description fits phloem sap, which is rich in sugars; xylem sap is mostly a watery solution.

options.label: A watery solution of hormones, minerals, and other nutrients
options.feedback: Correct. Xylem sap is primarily water carrying dissolved substances.

options.label: A milky white fluid with proteins
options.feedback: That sounds like latex, not xylem sap.

options.label: A sticky resin that hardens in air
options.feedback: Resin is not sap; xylem sap is a watery solution.

items.ok_line: Xylem sap is mostly water with dissolved nutrients.
items.ko_line: That is a different substance or the other sap type.
items.exp_text: Xylem sap is primarily a watery solution containing hormones, mineral elements, and other nutrients. It moves from the roots upward toward the leaves.

items.prompt: In which direction does xylem sap travel through a plant?

options.label: From the roots toward the leaves
options.feedback: Correct. Xylem sap moves upward from the roots to the leaves.

options.label: From the leaves toward the roots
options.feedback: That is the direction of phloem sap, not xylem sap.

options.label: From the trunk out to the branches and back
options.feedback: That is not accurate; xylem sap has a clear upward path from roots to leaves.

options.label: In all directions at once
options.feedback: No, xylem sap moves specifically from roots to leaves.

items.ok_line: Xylem sap goes up from roots to leaves.
items.ko_line: That is not how xylem sap moves.
items.exp_text: Xylem sap is transported from the roots upward toward the leaves. This movement is characteristic of xylem transport.

items.prompt: What does phloem sap mainly consist of?

options.label: A watery solution of minerals only
options.feedback: Phloem sap does contain minerals, but its main component is sugars.

options.label: A pure water with no dissolved substances
options.feedback: That is not correct; phloem sap is rich in dissolved sugars and other compounds.

options.label: Sugars, hormones, and mineral elements dissolved in water
options.feedback: Correct. The main component is sugars, mainly sucrose.

options.label: A thick, sticky resin
options.feedback: Resin is a separate substance, not phloem sap.

items.ok_line: Phloem sap is sugar-rich with hormones and minerals.
items.ko_line: That is not the main makeup of phloem sap.
items.exp_text: Phloem sap consists primarily of sugars, especially sucrose, along with hormones and mineral elements dissolved in water. It flows from where sugars are made or stored to where they are used.

items.prompt: Where does phloem sap flow from and to?

options.label: From roots to leaves
options.feedback: That is xylem sap's direction, not phloem sap's.

options.label: From leaves to other leaves only
options.feedback: Phloem sap moves from sugar sources to sugar sinks, not just leaf to leaf.

options.label: From the trunk to the roots and leaves equally
options.feedback: Phloem sap has a specific source-to-sink direction, not equal movement to all parts.

options.label: From where carbohydrates are produced or stored to where they are used
options.feedback: Correct. This is the sugar source to sugar sink flow.

items.ok_line: Phloem sap goes from source to sink.
items.ko_line: That is not the direction phloem sap takes.
items.exp_text: Phloem sap flows from sugar sources, where carbohydrates are made or stored, to sugar sinks, where they are used. This is opposite to the upward flow of xylem sap.

items.prompt: What can disrupt xylem sap transport by causing cavitation?

options.label: Too many nutrients in the soil
options.feedback: Nutrient excess is not mentioned as a cause of cavitation; the factors are water stress and freeze-thaw cycles.

options.label: Water stress and freeze-thaw cycles
options.feedback: Correct. These two environmental stresses can trigger cavitation.

options.label: Insects feeding on the leaves
options.feedback: Insects feeding is not listed as a cause of cavitation.

options.label: Lack of light reaching the leaves
options.feedback: Light shortage is not mentioned as causing cavitation.

items.ok_line: Water stress and freeze-thaw cause cavitation.
items.exp_text: Xylem sap transport can be disrupted by cavitation, where water abruptly changes from liquid to vapor, leaving air-filled conduits. This can be caused by increasingly negative xylem pressures from water stress and by freeze-thaw cycles in temperate climates.

items.prompt: What is honeydew, sometimes called sap when it falls from trees?

options.label: The sap that trees produce in spring
options.feedback: Honeydew is not tree-produced sap; it comes from insects.

options.label: A type of resin that drips from bark
options.feedback: Honeydew is not resin; it is insect waste.

options.label: The remains of eaten sap and other plant parts that insects excrete
options.feedback: Correct. Honeydew is the leftover after insects feed on sap.

options.label: The sugary liquid inside a flower
options.feedback: That is nectar, not honeydew.

items.ok_line: Honeydew is insect waste from eaten sap.
items.ko_line: That is a different plant or insect product.
items.exp_text: Honeydew is called sap, especially when it falls from trees, but it is actually the remains of sap and other plant parts that insects have eaten and excreted. It is not true sap.

items.prompt: Which insects feed directly on phloem sap?

options.label: Insects of the order Hemiptera
options.feedback: Correct. Many Hemiptera, also called half-wings, feed directly on phloem sap.

options.label: Beetles
options.feedback: Beetles are not mentioned; the order is Hemiptera.

options.label: Butterflies and moths
options.feedback: Those belong to Lepidoptera, not Hemiptera.

options.label: Ants
options.feedback: Ants are not cited as direct phloem feeders; the order is Hemiptera.

items.ko_line: Those are not the direct phloem sap feeders.
items.exp_text: Many insects of the order Hemiptera feed directly on phloem sap, making it a primary part of their diet. These insects have special adaptations to handle the high sugar content and osmotic pressure.

items.prompt: What is maple syrup made from?

options.label: Phloem sap of maple trees
options.feedback: Maple syrup is made from xylem sap, not phloem sap.

options.label: Resin from maple bark
options.feedback: Resin is not the source; it is xylem sap.

options.label: Honeydew from maple-feeding insects
options.feedback: Honeydew is not used; the sap is from the tree itself.

options.label: Reduced xylem sap of the sugar maple
options.feedback: Correct. Maple syrup comes from concentrating sugar maple xylem sap.

items.ok_line: Maple syrup is from sugar maple xylem sap.
items.ko_line: That is not what maple syrup is made from.
items.exp_text: Maple syrup is made by reducing the xylem sap of the sugar maple, Acer saccharum. The sap is harvested and boiled down to concentrate its sugars.
